question: Can a declared Appendix-B-inspired prefix-Keraia weak-head profile expose resumable read boundaries, transport input-free segments with exact cost, and reproduce exhaustive halting-code mass by prefix search?
level: External finite interpreter and receipt calibration; no native Adva semantics
source: Michael Stay, Very simple Chaitin machines for concrete AIT, arXiv:cs/0508056, sections 8-9 and Appendix B, read including page images
semantics: The first complete ordered binary tree is program and the remaining bits are data
Greedy structural variable marking follows Appendix B; independently compare its string-replacement formulation
Call-by-name weak-head evaluation; do not reduce beneath a returned lambda
Applying R to x consumes one bit: 0 returns K x, 1 returns I
Exact finite input is accepted only on weak-head return with no unread suffix
cost: One application-spine push, beta contraction, primitive read or final weak-head return costs one semantic step. Waiting for input and externally appending one requested bit cost no semantic step. Compilation, tree/term traversal and receipt verification are separately counted host work. No resumption or cache hit renews semantic fuel.

fixtures: paper one-read example with empty/0/1/10 suffix
K I applied to the loop

interface: Exact closed de Bruijn control term, ordered argument stack, absolute input cursor, evaluation profile and cost convention form a read-free segment boundary. A checked segment never consumes input or overwrites source word, read history or probability weight. Histories and per-code provenance remain outside the cache and are copied on branching.
checks: Independent tree/string compilers agree on all parsed family members
Independent named-substitution oracle agrees on full-budget outputs, read order and consumed input
Direct and checked-cache ledgers agree at all time cuts
Resumable prefix traversal finds exactly the same accepted codes and exact dyadic mass
Accepted codes plus unresolved prefix cylinders form a Kraft partition
Checkpoint replay binds receiver-selected source, profile and original fuel; altered cursor, residual, read trace or fuel is rejected
Altered segment profile/cursor/cost/endpoint is refused; original cost is debited on a cache hit
Input and branch snapshots have independent ownership
Compare the printed section-8 K and Appendix-B K without silently changing either
All four retained integer-versus-bool/float checkpoint and receipt failures are refused
protected: UnknownFuel is not a proof of divergence
Weak-head return is not full normalization
No transfer of optimal universality or Chaitin randomness to this observation profile
No native Q4/M6, SourceId, Seal or library admission
enforcement: All tree, term, evaluator and checker loops consume a shared counted-work/deadline guard. Term and stack sizes are capped. The supervisor imposes subprocess timeout plus prlimit CPU/address-space/output limits, retains failures and compares one fresh successful replay. No automatic correction or scope expansion; a necessary correction must be recorded before its invocation.
exit: A completed fixed family, source/profile discrepancy, checker mismatch, explicit limit or implementation failure. Retain source discrepancies as results; do not silently repair source examples. Stop after the declared attempt; corrections require a written continuation record.
